Episode 183. A Preliminary Battle Started From Within (3)
The Labyrinth Master had two exclusive closed-door training rooms.
One was the 'Labyrinth within the Labyrinth', accessible only through the powers of Manbing and Mort, and the other was at the top level of the Labyrinth.
The space Syris was about to open was the latter.
The former was limited in access because Syris was not yet adept at handling Manbing, and currently, Elona Jiepli was sealed inside.

Opening the Labyrinth within the Labyrinth clumsily could provoke Misha and Elona, causing problems, and more importantly, it was a place where quick responses from the outside would be impossible if anything happened to Jin.
[Booong!]
Syris placed Jin on top of Mort. The pulse he felt from Jin's wrist, which he held to lift him up, was incredibly weak.
'Undoubtedly, the mental attack Jin is undergoing must be on a completely different level than what I or anyone else is experiencing....'
As Syris thought, the mental attack that people other than Jin were experiencing was several stages lower.
Syris felt a deep admiration for Jin, who not only endured such attacks with poise until now, but also was now preparing to fight completely alone.
Mort went outside and slowly crawled up the wall of the Labyrinth.
Although he intended to teleport, even the natural turbulence from running through the different world of the Snowfield seemed to be a blow to Jin's current state.
Jin was, more than ever, in a weakened condition.
In the meantime, his companions including Valeria and Qwaul, and the members of the Labyrinth, went up to the top level of the Labyrinth first to wait for Jin.
Eventually, Mort reached the top level.
Jin, who had dismounted from Mort's back, took a deep breath. The air was so cold that it stung his lungs, but Jin could hardly feel such sensations.
His senses in the real world were extremely dull. His vision was blurry, he could hardly hear, and there was absolutely no strength in his arms and legs.
Watching Jin, supported by Gilly and walking, the companions couldn't help but worry if it was okay to send such a person to the closed-door training room alone.
Jin looked at his companions who appeared blurry in his field of vision.
"Master...."
Gilly's voice was trembling, wet with emotion. It was painful to see Jin exhausted to his limit.
"Looks like everyone's been waiting."
Jin wanted to say this in his usual confident voice. He wanted to tell them not to worry too much and just wait.
But now, he wanted to share a little more of his honest feelings.
"If five days pass and I don't come out of the training room. Then I have lost. And that would mean my death."
At this point, Gilly could no longer hold back her tears.
Valeria bit her lower lip and patted her back.
For a while, no one could say anything.
"Honestly, I'm not sure if I can win. But I won't leave any last words. I don't want a sad farewell as if it's definitely the end. Because there's a real final battle after this fight."
Jin sent a wink to Syris. It meant to open the door to the closed-door training room.
When Syris pulled out the Manbing and plugged it into the door like a key, a pure white energy flowed out from the inside of the training room like a wave.
When the door opened, a wide expanse of cold, pure white ground was revealed.
"So, it can't end here...."
Jin slowly moved his steps beyond, walking heavily. He was pressing the ground with his staff-like Bradamante.
The small bag containing minimal food seemed incredibly heavy.
His senses in the real world were dulling by the second. He hadn't taken many steps, but already, his companions behind him felt far away.
"Jin! Come back safely. I'm holding up well against the mental attacks, so you can definitely win! When you come back, I'll share my eel porridge!"
Surprisingly, the first one to shout, and in very precise pronunciation, was none other than Darkflame.
Darkflame was the only one among the small numbers in the Labyrinth who had experienced mental attacks.
"W-what, what, what! Why is that guy suddenly speaking so well!?"
Pengi shouted in surprise.
Even the solemn companions were taken aback by the sudden, precise, and fast voice of Darkflame.
"I'll share the eel soup! Eel soup....!"
"Hey, Darkflame! Are you okay? Huh? No, you could speak properly from the start, right....no, you're not okay."
"I'll share the eel soup!"
Pengi, grabbing Darkflame's shoulder, realized that Darkflame was now closing his eyes tightly due to the pain of the mental attack.
Amidst the confusion, he had shouted loudly for Jin, and it just happened to be pronounced precisely and quickly.
Darkflame is clearly the weakest person in this labyrinth. But he was also trying so hard.
Darkflame's shout of sharing the eel soup continued like a chorus. His companions could not see it, and Jin himself did not realize it. But Jin smiled faintly at the sound.
As Jin fully stepped into the closed-door training room, Syris closed the door with a heavy face.
Now there was only one thing his comrades could do for Jin.
They wished for his victory. Just like the many ordinary people in the world.
Inside the training room was pure white, but to Jin, it looked like a dark sea without a single light.
He could not tell if he was standing, sitting, or lying down.
But what was important to Jin now was not reality. The inner battlefield, which had been fiercely continuous without a moment's rest, was more important.
So he had to sink deeper within. To the extent that the sense of reality was completely wiped out without a trace.
This was why he chose the closed-door training room. He needed a space where he could concentrate on the inner battlefield without even the slightest external stimulus.
Jin was carefully sinking. Towards his inner world.
It's like walking the line between life and death.
One misstep, and oblivion and death will befall Jin.
'Do you think that's right?'
'Do you think that method is correct?'
'So, do you think you can reach me?'
'Can you save those many people from me?'
Every now and then, Rosa's voice could be heard as he moved towards his inner world.
Each time that dark voice shook his ego, he shivered in anxiety.
He regretted it. He wanted to turn back right away.
The closer he got to the inner world, the greater the fear grew.
A massive fear, like nothing Jin had ever experienced in his previous or current life, was overwhelming his ego.
'It's the first time I've seen you trembling in fear.'
'What you see is the first time, but it has happened often.'
'Is that so?'
'You would have had those moments when you were a human too.'
'I've never succumbed to fear. So you show me, too, that you can do the same.'
At first, Jin thought he would fight alone to do so.
However, the deeper he delved into his inner world, the faster Jin realized.
In this desolate and lonely world, to overcome fear, he would have to become a monster just like Rosa.
Without becoming a monster of at least that degree, he could not but succumb to the fear of the loneliness of the inner world.
A single white line came into Jin's field of view.
Jin intuitively recognized that it was a kind of door leading to the deepest part of the inner world.
Beyond that, Rosa's ego would be waiting for him.
And that white line was also a crossroad of choices.
The result would change depending on the mindset he pulls it with.
If he pulls it with the intention to become a monster, he will become a monster, and if he wants to remain human, it will just open.
'But to remain human...'
'You can't beat me.'
Rosa was now seeing through Jin's thoughts like past Lingling. It was because his ego touching the inner world was getting closer.

'By now, you can read my thoughts, too, my son. This inner battle is a gift I prepared for you. Before the end, this mother wanted to make you a more perfect being. An entity that can fight equally with me.'
Open the door with the intention of becoming a monster. That's the only hope you have to beat me.
Rosa was saying so.
Jin gripped the white line. Looking back once, the path of the inner world he had descended so far was shattering and flying like dust.
Just as he was about to pull it with the intention of becoming a monster, Jin suddenly stopped in surprise.
It was because of the rustling noise in his ear.
It wasn't Rosa's gloomy voice, but the wishes of the people outside whispering like whispers were tickling Jin's ears.
Jin couldn't hear the content at all. It was just a feeling like a cool wind blowing in his ears, but it was enough to make Jin think once again.
'I was about to throw away the one thing that makes me superior to you in order to oppose you, even if that means becoming like you.'
Because people have a feeling of fear, they protect themselves from danger.
You can run away when you're afraid, and you can respond properly when you're scared.
Fighting back while struggling with fear was the human way.
'Even if I become a monster and break you... It just results in another monstrous figure appearing in the world.'
Due to the long mental attack, Jin, whose ego was devastated, was missing that obvious fact.
Jin, who had drawn a conclusion, cautiously pulled the white line.
And what was revealed when the door opened was not Rosa's ego.
It was not an empty void or vague darkness. It was the back view of a man sitting.
"Father...?"
It was Chiron Runcandel, Jin's father. The reason he stood where Rosa's ego should have been was that Jin had not become a monster.
"Jin."
He had never missed his father as desperately as he did these days.
Strength filled his feeble limbs again, and it felt like hot blood was filling his foggy head. Jin was running toward Chiron without realizing it.
But he couldn't reach Chiron.
A cliff, deep and huge like a sea, separated Jin and Chiron.
When Jin stopped at the edge of the cliff, Chiron looked back.
It was indeed his father's face, which he hadn't seen in a long time.
The father and son stared into each other's eyes for a while.
"You endured well."
At Chiron's single uttered word, Jin was suddenly able to realize.
In this inner world, which was simply lonely and painful, Chiron had been watching over him from the beginning to the end.
"There will be a day when we meet again."
With those words, Chiron turned around and started to walk.
As if to say let's go back to our own battlegrounds now.
Jin watched his father walking toward somewhere deeper and darker for a long time.
It didn't seem to fit the moment to add something more to his father.
As Chiron's figure disappeared and Jin looked back again, he could see that the inner world paths that had collapsed before were forming again.
Jin, like Chiron, silently walked up that path.
When Jin escaped the inner world and regained his sense of reality.
The day was breaking outside, and Rosa's mental attack that had plunged the world into pain was completely gone.
Jin, more energetic than ever, opened the door to the training hall with all his might.
